title: Israel Orders West Bank Lockdown Following Deadly Shooting Near Hebron Ahead of High-Stakes Election
snippet: Tensions soar in the occupied West Bank as Israeli forces kill two armed Palestinians near Hebron, prompting Prime Minister Netanyahu to order a full closure of the territory days before a crucial vote.
content:
HEBRON, West Bank — Israeli security forces shot and killed two Palestinian men Friday after an alleged attack near the city of Hebron, sparking fresh violence and leading Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to order a complete lockdown of the occupied West Bank just days before Israel's national election.

According to the Israeli military, soldiers intercepted two men armed with an M16 rifle and a handgun, preventing what officials termed a "major terror attack against civilians." At least five people sustained injuries during the incident, with some in critical condition, emergency personnel reported.

Political Fallout Ahead of Election

The escalation comes at a pivotal political moment for Israel, as voters head to the polls on Tuesday to decide whether to grant Netanyahu another term in office. The election coincides with heightened national anxiety leading up to the anniversary of the October 7 attack that ignited the ongoing war in Gaza.

In response to the shooting, Netanyahu convened an emergency session of his Security Cabinet, claiming that intelligence indicated Hamas was orchestrating a widespread effort to target innocent civilians ahead of the vote. "Our brave soldiers thwarted this attack with courage and determination," Netanyahu stated, praising the military's swift intervention.

Widespread Security Operations and Crackdowns

Far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir immediately advocated for further restricting Palestinian movement throughout the region, arguing that security must take precedence over local mobility. Meanwhile, Israeli intelligence and military forces executed a series of raids across the West Bank, detaining dozens of individuals allegedly linked to militant factions and seizing various caches of weapons and ammunition.

The impending lockdown marks the fourth blanket restriction imposed on the West Bank in recent weeks. Under these measures, checkpoints connecting Palestinian towns are shut down, severely disrupting daily life, while Israeli citizens and settlers generally maintain access to main arterial roads.

Critics, including visiting U.S. Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander, denounced the sweeping closures as an excessive measure that inflicts heavy restrictions on Palestinians. Conversely, local conservative leaders maintained that stringent control measures are necessary to ensure public safety amid escalating regional instability.
